status.en: 194 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 21% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Plateau State and Lagos.
status.nb: 194 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 21 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Plateau State og Lagos.

summary.en: Bandits ambushed military-escorted traders in Zamfara, killing dozens and also killing eight security operatives and 12 traders in a separate attack. ISWAP fighters launched an assault on a town in Borno but were repelled, with over 40 militants killed in air strikes. Kidnappers in Kaduna abducted a couple and their infant, demanding a N300 million ransom and releasing a video of the family. Atiku Abubakar called on security agencies to rescue the abducted family. The conflict caused 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter overfalt handelsmenn med militær eskortering i Zamfara, drepte dusinvis og drepte også åtte sikkerhetsoperatører og 12 handelsmenn i et separat angrep. ISWAP-krigere lanserte et angrep på en by i Borno, men ble avverget, med over 40 militante drept i luftangrep. Kidnapperne i Kaduna bortførte et par og deres spedbarn, krevde en løsepenger på N300 millioner og slapp en video av familien. Atiku Abubakar oppfordret sikkerhetsbyråene til å redde den bortførte familien. Konflikten forårsaket 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
